CRLA No. 372 of 2021
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Vaibhav Singh Chauhan,
Advocate for the appellants.
Mr. S.S. Adhikari, D.A.G., for the 
State.
The appellants Vipin Kumar and 
Virendra have been convicted and 
sentenced under Section 307 read 
with 34 and 326 read with 34 IPC on 
23.09.2021, in Sessions Trial No. 62 of 
2016, by the Court of 2nd Additional 
Sessions Judge, Roorkee, District 
Haridwar.
Heard on Bail Application No. 2 of 
2021.
Learned counsel for the 
appellants would submit that the 
scribe of the FIR has not been 
examined. The person, who was 
informed about the incident by the 
victim, after the incident, has also not 
been examined. The FIR is delayed. 
Though, PW4 Ramesh Singh would 
submit that he had informed the family 
members of the victim and the Police 
as well on the date of incident itself. In 
addition, it is also argued that the 
medical examination does not support 
the oral evidence.
According to the FIR, in the late 
evening on 17.08.2015, the victim was 
attacked by co-convicts Sonu and 
other persons. The charge sheet was 
submitted against the appellants also. 
In evidence, the victim as PW2 has 
stated that he was attacked with a 
sharp edged weapon by the appellants 
also.
The victim has stated about the 
incident. There are eyewitnesses. PW3 Dr. Tasdiq Khan and PW9 Dr. Arvind 
Verma have stated about the injuries,
which were found grievous in nature. 
In fact, there were fractures on the face 
itself. The evidence was found reliable 
by the court below.
Having considered the entirety of 
facts, this Court is of the view that it is 
not a fit case for bail.
The bail application is rejected.
Paper book is ready. Let it be 
provided to learned counsel for the 
appellant.
List for final hearing.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 24.12.2021 Jitendra

IA 6/2026 (For second bail application)
Vipin Kumar And Another
--Appellant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Akshay Pradhan, learned counsel for the 
applicant.
2. Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, learned A.G.A. for the 
State.
3. The instant appeal is an admitted appeal, 
admitted on 24.11.2021 and the Trial Court record is 
summoned and the paper book is also ready. The 
appellant herein namely Vipin Kumar is already 
enlarged on bail on 10.12.2024 and now the bail 
application is moved on behalf of appellant no. 2-
Virendra. The Trial Court convicted both the 
appellants for the offences punishable under sections 
307 read with 34 of IPC with the maximum sentence of 
7 years imprisonment with the fine of Rs. 10,000/-.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the 
appellant on the basis of the jail custody certificate 
dated 18.04.2026 of District Jail, Haridwar, that the 
present appellant served more than half of the 
sentence since as on 18.04.2026 as he has served 5 years 
4 months 1 day without remission and 5 years 9 
months 13 days with remission.
5. Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, learned A.G.A. have not 
raised any objection with regard to the long 
incarceration of the appellant and he also fairly 
submits on the basis of the custody certificate that the 
appellant no. 2 already served more than half of the 
sentence. 6. After hearing the submission of learned counsel 
for the parties and taking into consideration the 
custody certificate dated 18.04.2026 of Jailor of District 
Jail, Haridwar, since the appellant no. 2 already served 
more than half of the sentence, this court is of the view 
that the appellant no. 2 deserves for bail.
7. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on 
the merit of the case the bail application of appellant 
no. 2 is allowed.
8. Let the appellant no. 2 ‘Virendra’ be enlarged on 
bail on furnishing his personal bond and two reliable 
sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of 
the court concerned during the pendency of the instant 
criminal appeal.
9. List this appeal in the month of November, 2026
for final disposal.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 20.08.2026
PR
